interest: Shows 1947 Army-State clash over zaibatsu dissolution, with Marshall managing Royall's objections and MacArthur's defense of the policy.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file comprises Department of State records from November 1947 concerning United States policy on the deconcentration of excessive economic power in occupied Japan (the Zaibatsu program) and the emerging interdepartmental rift between the State Department and Secretary of the Army Kenneth C. Royall. Royall questioned the dissolution program as potentially 'un-American', punitive, and harmful to Japanese industrial recovery, and proposed appointing an independent committee of prominent private citizens, including former Secretary of War Henry L. Stimson, to reconsider the policy. The file includes a comprehensive November 19, 1947 briefing memorandum prepared by Frank G. Wisner for Secretary of State George C. Marshall defending General Douglas MacArthur's implementation of anti-monopoly legislation, an informal transmittal note from the Under Secretary's office, and a November 20, 1947 memorandum of conversation detailing Secretary Marshall's guidance to revise the memorandum into a strictly factual, non-argumentative review to be presented to Royall by Under Secretary Robert A. Lovett, while differentiating the Japanese deconcentration efforts from General Lucius D. Clay's policies in occupied Germany.

subfiles.about: Provides a comprehensive background summary and defense of the Zaibatsu deconcentration program in Japan to answer objections raised by Secretary of the Army Kenneth C. Royall.
subfiles.from: Charles F. Saltzman (by Frank G. Wisner, Deputy to the Assistant Secretary for Occupied Areas)
subfiles.summary: Wisner defends zaibatsu dissolution to Marshall against Royall's objections, warning a review committee would unsettle recovery, and urges backing MacArthur's pending Anti-Monopoly Ordinance.
